# awesome-tv-debloat

Every way to strip ads off a smart TV, listed by brand.

## Safety

ADB and similar debug tools can leave a television without a home screen, without inputs, or without updates. Prefer the Start here row for that brand. Write down package names before disabling anything, and keep the project's own way back. This list is not a set of instructions, and it does not claim that these projects were run on a television here. Every cell comes from that project's README or code. The link on the cell is that page. Where the project is silent, the cell says unknown.

## How to read this

Root is yes, no, or depends. Undo is yes, partial, or no, followed by the way back the project describes. PC is whether a computer is required. unknown means that project's README or code does not say. Stars and the last commit date come from the GitHub API. A project that is not hosted on GitHub has unknown in those two cells. The license is an SPDX identifier taken from the project's license file, or unknown when no license is stated. Kind is one or more of DNS blocking, clean launcher, ad-free client, ADB debloat, homebrew, and firmware / root.

## Google TV and Android TV

**Start here: [Tellyscope](https://github.com/man15h/tellyscope)** by [man15h](https://github.com/man15h). The README says the phone app needs no root and no computer, disables built-in apps instead of uninstalling them, keeps a protected list, and can turn back on only what it turned off. [src](https://github.com/man15h/tellyscope/blob/main/README.md)

Notes

- **Tellyscope.** Phone app. The README names Android TV, Google TV, NVIDIA Shield and Fire TV, and says a real-hardware check for Shield and Fire TV is still open. Tweaks include ad-blocking Private DNS, and it can install a launcher.
- **Aerial.** tvOS-style Android TV launcher aimed at Xiaomi, TCL, Skyworth, Sony and other sets, including a Hisense model in the device table. System apps are not modified. Install paths include a computer, and a USB stick without one.
- **Free My TV.** One home screen for Google TV, LG webOS and Samsung Tizen. The Google TV path also turns off the stock home and some named packages, without uninstalling them. A webOS Homebrew Channel repository can skip the computer. TCL, Hisense and Xiaomi remote-button behavior is described in the same README.
- **Quiet TV.** Android TV launcher for China-market sets, based on CleanYourTV, with no ads and no recommendation row. Day-to-day layout does not need ADB. First-time setup and boot-ad handling are described as a computer step. The README says no root and no firmware flash.
- **Tigris.** Android TV launcher that names Xiaomi, TCL, Hisense and Skyworth, and says it does not root, does not change system partitions, and does not uninstall the factory desktop. A USB install can open the basic desktop. The webOS tree is described as a development preview, and Home-button takeover is not a finished release.
- **CleanYourTV.** Computer, or a coding assistant on that computer, for Android TV and Google TV. On Fire TV the README says only the debloat half applies. Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku, Vizio and Hisense VIDAA are named as unsupported. The brand table includes Xiaomi, TCL and Hisense Android sets.
- **Projectivy installer.** Windows and Linux wizards for Projectivy on a Fire TV Stick running Fire OS 7 or 8. The README says nothing in the tool needs root, and that it does not use the hidden API blacklist exemption. Optional Private DNS is documented. A Sony BRAVIA note is in the same README.
- **SmartTube.** Media client for Android TVs and TV boxes. The FAQ says SmartTube has no code to display ads. Supported devices include Fire TV released before October 2025. The README says it does not run on Samsung Tizen, LG webOS or Roku, and that the Fire TV Stick 4K Select and newer VegaOS sticks are out of scope. The easiest install named is the Downloader app on the TV.
- **Projectivy Launcher.** Ad-free Android TV launcher, installed from Google Play or the GitHub releases. The same README says rooting, custom recovery, disabling stock apps and replacing the launcher remain available in version 4.x, and that the files cover a few Xiaomi-ecosystem devices. No license file was found.
- **Clean Your TV app.** Android phone app for the CleanYourTV lists. The README says Fire TV, TCL China builds and Android 7 get cleanup only, and that a new home screen is limited to models whose list says the switch holds. It never uses the word root.
- **TV Home.** XMB-style home installed with adb. The README does not say whether root is required, and it does not name a license. A Hisense section hides com.vt.* apps from the list, and DISABLED_PACKAGES.txt is described as including two Hisense analytics services on the author's set.
- **简居 TV.** Mainland-app home screen forked from Aerial at a named commit. The README says it has no ad slots and does not change DNS, and that in-app ads inside video apps stay the platform's. It does not say whether root is required. Install notes name a Xiaomi MiTV-MFTR0 and say other brands are outside that note.
- **LTvLauncher.** Fork of FLauncher. The README calls it ad-free and names Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV. The Downloader app path does not use a computer. The README does not say whether root is required.
- **FLauncher.** Open-source Android TV launcher on GitLab, so GitHub stars and the GitHub last-commit date are unknown. The feature list includes no ads. Play Store is one install path. The README does not say whether root is required.
- **homehound.** Minimal launcher for Fire TV and Android TV. The repository name is lobby. The debloat script disables the Amazon packages in debloat-list.txt and says nothing is uninstalled. Root and a license are not stated. Setup is an adb script or an on-TV accessibility toggle.
- **TV Detox.** A small home screen plus a prompt for a coding assistant. The README says apps are turned off, never deleted, and that the assistant has to run on a computer on the same network. It does not say whether root is required. Philips and TCL behavior is called out in the same file.
- **TizenTube Cobalt.** Android client from the TizenTube author. The README says it removes ads and adds SponsorBlock, and that a Google TV certified device is the preferred target. Install is sideload via a file manager, ADB, or a platform-specific method.

Notes

- **Hearth.** Fire OS 7 or 8 home screen. Amazon's launcher stays enabled. SKIP_DEBLOAT=1 skips package cleanup. DNS=1 is optional AdGuard Private DNS. The model table names TCL, Hisense, Insignia, Xiaomi and Toshiba Fire TV sets. The repository description says no root.
- **Tellyscope.** Phone app. The README names Android TV, Google TV, NVIDIA Shield and Fire TV, and says a real-hardware check for Shield and Fire TV is still open. Tweaks include ad-blocking Private DNS, and it can install a launcher.
- **CleanYourTV.** Computer, or a coding assistant on that computer, for Android TV and Google TV. On Fire TV the README says only the debloat half applies. Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku, Vizio and Hisense VIDAA are named as unsupported. The brand table includes Xiaomi, TCL and Hisense Android sets.
- **dumbtv.** Fire TV stick, Cube or Fire TV Edition set, from a computer. The device list names Hisense, Xiaomi, TCL, Insignia and Toshiba Fire TV Edition models. The DNS filter is described as blocking Fire OS updates while it runs. The launcher can be installed on its own. Code is MIT. The device catalog is CC BY-SA 4.0.
- **fire-tv-debloat.** ADB scripts for one Insignia NS-43DF710 Fire TV Edition set. debloat.sh uninstalls for the current user or disables packages, and a protected-package guard is described. No license is stated.
- **Projectivy installer.** Windows and Linux wizards for Projectivy on a Fire TV Stick running Fire OS 7 or 8. The README says nothing in the tool needs root, and that it does not use the hidden API blacklist exemption. Optional Private DNS is documented. A Sony BRAVIA note is in the same README.
- **Clean your Fire TV.** Prompt and optional launcher for Fire TV, adapted from CleanYourTV and separately maintained. The README says it does not root the TV or uninstall system packages, and that the prompt does not disable packages by itself. On the AFTT stick it describes, Fire OS rejected disabling manufacturer packages and the Home button stayed on Amazon Home.
- **SmartTube.** Media client for Android TVs and TV boxes. The FAQ says SmartTube has no code to display ads. Supported devices include Fire TV released before October 2025. The README says it does not run on Samsung Tizen, LG webOS or Roku, and that the Fire TV Stick 4K Select and newer VegaOS sticks are out of scope. The easiest install named is the Downloader app on the TV.
- **Clean Your TV app.** Android phone app for the CleanYourTV lists. The README says Fire TV, TCL China builds and Android 7 get cleanup only, and that a new home screen is limited to models whose list says the switch holds. It never uses the word root.
- **LTvLauncher.** Fork of FLauncher. The README calls it ad-free and names Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV. The Downloader app path does not use a computer. The README does not say whether root is required.
- **homehound.** Minimal launcher for Fire TV and Android TV. The repository name is lobby. The debloat script disables the Amazon packages in debloat-list.txt and says nothing is uninstalled. Root and a license are not stated. Setup is an adb script or an on-TV accessibility toggle.

- **Free My TV for webOS.** Separate LG webOS home screen from simbasjungles/free-my-tv. The README says no root, stock Developer Mode or the Homebrew Channel, and that a computer does not have to stay on after install. First install is a computer or an Android phone.
- **Tigris.** Android TV launcher that names Xiaomi, TCL, Hisense and Skyworth, and says it does not root, does not change system partitions, and does not uninstall the factory desktop. A USB install can open the basic desktop. The webOS tree is described as a development preview, and Home-button takeover is not a finished release.
- **YouTube Ad-Free for webOS.** webOS YouTube client with ad blocking and SponsorBlock. This repository is a fork of FriedChickenButt/youtube-webos. Requirements say to uninstall the official YouTube app first. They do not say the replacement itself needs root.
- **CleanYourTV for webOS.** Home screen for rooted LG webOS 5 and newer, with an optional debloat of LG ads and telemetry. Install is the Homebrew Channel on the TV, or one SSH command from a computer. Default branch is dev.
- **Life's Good Without Spying.** Homebrew app for a rooted LG webOS 4 or newer TV. It sinkholes LG ad, ACR and telemetry domains and stops the on-TV ad and ACR daemons. The README does not say whether install needs a computer.
- **webOS Homebrew Channel.** Unofficial webOS package repository and root-related tooling. The feature list includes a root-only switch for some telemetry. Other webOS rows use it as the on-TV installer. The README does not say a computer is mandatory. ares-install and an on-TV curl snippet are both listed.

Notes

- **Aerial.** tvOS-style Android TV launcher aimed at Xiaomi, TCL, Skyworth, Sony and other sets, including a Hisense model in the device table. System apps are not modified. Install paths include a computer, and a USB stick without one.
- **Free My TV.** One home screen for Google TV, LG webOS and Samsung Tizen. The Google TV path also turns off the stock home and some named packages, without uninstalling them. A webOS Homebrew Channel repository can skip the computer. TCL, Hisense and Xiaomi remote-button behavior is described in the same README.
- **Quiet TV.** Android TV launcher for China-market sets, based on CleanYourTV, with no ads and no recommendation row. Day-to-day layout does not need ADB. First-time setup and boot-ad handling are described as a computer step. The README says no root and no firmware flash.
- **Tigris.** Android TV launcher that names Xiaomi, TCL, Hisense and Skyworth, and says it does not root, does not change system partitions, and does not uninstall the factory desktop. A USB install can open the basic desktop. The webOS tree is described as a development preview, and Home-button takeover is not a finished release.
- **CleanYourTV.** Computer, or a coding assistant on that computer, for Android TV and Google TV. On Fire TV the README says only the debloat half applies. Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku, Vizio and Hisense VIDAA are named as unsupported. The brand table includes Xiaomi, TCL and Hisense Android sets.
- **dumbtv.** Fire TV stick, Cube or Fire TV Edition set, from a computer. The device list names Hisense, Xiaomi, TCL, Insignia and Toshiba Fire TV Edition models. The DNS filter is described as blocking Fire OS updates while it runs. The launcher can be installed on its own. Code is MIT. The device catalog is CC BY-SA 4.0.
- **DumbTV HDMI.** HDMI-first home for one TCL Google TV on Android 12. It disables Google TV Home and does not describe an ad-domain list. The README says no root. No license is stated. The name clashes with humblemuzzu/dumbtv, which is a different project.
- **fire-tv-debloat.** ADB scripts for one Insignia NS-43DF710 Fire TV Edition set. debloat.sh uninstalls for the current user or disables packages, and a protected-package guard is described. No license is stated.
- **Hearth.** Fire OS 7 or 8 home screen. Amazon's launcher stays enabled. SKIP_DEBLOAT=1 skips package cleanup. DNS=1 is optional AdGuard Private DNS. The model table names TCL, Hisense, Insignia, Xiaomi and Toshiba Fire TV sets. The repository description says no root.
- **Redmi TV Toolkit.** No-root helper for MiTV-ASTR0 / blueplanet. The README says it does not unlock the bootloader or change system partitions, and that other firmware is refused unless the override switch in the README is passed. It installs Projectivy from spocky/miproja1 releases. The documented computer is Windows with PowerShell 7.
- **Projectivy Launcher.** Ad-free Android TV launcher, installed from Google Play or the GitHub releases. The same README says rooting, custom recovery, disabling stock apps and replacing the launcher remain available in version 4.x, and that the files cover a few Xiaomi-ecosystem devices. No license file was found.
- **Clean Your TV app.** Android phone app for the CleanYourTV lists. The README says Fire TV, TCL China builds and Android 7 get cleanup only, and that a new home screen is limited to models whose list says the switch holds. It never uses the word root.
- **tcl-tv-detox.** Write-up for one TCL 32S5500, plus a patched TV Detox home so HDMI tiles reach TCL's own player. It is not a general installer. The home screen credits Ansub's MIT license. This repository does not state its own license or whether root is required.
- **TV Home.** XMB-style home installed with adb. The README does not say whether root is required, and it does not name a license. A Hisense section hides com.vt.* apps from the list, and DISABLED_PACKAGES.txt is described as including two Hisense analytics services on the author's set.
- **简居 TV.** Mainland-app home screen forked from Aerial at a named commit. The README says it has no ad slots and does not change DNS, and that in-app ads inside video apps stay the platform's. It does not say whether root is required. Install notes name a Xiaomi MiTV-MFTR0 and say other brands are outside that note.
- **TV Detox.** A small home screen plus a prompt for a coding assistant. The README says apps are turned off, never deleted, and that the assistant has to run on a computer on the same network. It does not say whether root is required. Philips and TCL behavior is called out in the same file.

- **Pi-hole.** DNS sinkhole the README describes as network-wide ad blocking, including smart TVs, with no client software on the television. It runs on the owner's Linux hardware. The Roku list below is meant to be added to it. GitHub's license field is NOASSERTION. The license file states EUPL-1.2.

## Related lists

[Awesome Android TV FOSS Apps](https://github.com/Generator/Awesome-Android-TV-FOSS-Apps) is a separate curated list of free and open-source Android TV apps. This repository does not copy its wording or its layout.

## Left out of v1

These came up while gathering the tables. They are omitted because a cell would have been a guess, or because the project is not itself a way to strip ads.

- [NextDNS CLI](https://github.com/nextdns/nextdns). The README describes a DNS-over-HTTPS client for routers and desktops. It does not say the client blocks ads, and it does not mention televisions.
- [samsung-tizen-tv-debloat](https://github.com/ardazeytin/samsung-tizen-tv-debloat). The README says sdb cannot remove the ads, and that the steps which do cut ads are remote settings rather than this tool.
- [personalDNSfilter](https://github.com/IngoZenz/personaldnsfilter). The README is only a pointer to an external site, so root, undo and television scope are not stated in the repository. dumbtv documents the copy it runs.
- [webOS Dev Manager](https://github.com/webosbrew/dev-manager-desktop). Desktop tool for developer mode and rooted webOS. It installs packages and does not itself remove ads. The YouTube webOS row links it as an install path.
- [Firestick Cleaner and Launcher Replacer](https://github.com/niftiest/Firestick-Cleaner-And-Launcher-Replacer). Overlaps the Projectivy installer row. That row is the one whose README states an undo log.
- [uveer18/xiaomitv](https://github.com/uveer18/xiaomitv). The README follows the CleanYourTV prompt and launcher, and the license file keeps Gathin's copyright, so it is not a separate Xiaomi tool.
- [SmartTubeLegacy](https://github.com/yuliskov/SmartTubeLegacy). GitHub marks the repository archived. SmartTube is the current project.
- [Apps2Samsung](https://github.com/Apps2Samsung/Apps2Samsung). Named by TizenTube's install guide as the installer. Its own root and undo statements were not reviewed, so it has no row.
- [Awesome Android TV FOSS Apps](https://github.com/Generator/Awesome-Android-TV-FOSS-Apps). Linked under Related lists. Its text and layout are not reused, and it is a general app list rather than a brand-by-brand ad-strip table.
- [Hisense VIDAA, Vizio, and Roku beyond DNS](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/blob/main/README.md). CleanYourTV's README says VIDAA, Vizio and Roku have no ADB path. No other public README in this pass stated a reversible on-device tool for VIDAA or Vizio. Roku is only the hosts list above.
- [Country forks and skins](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv). Forks and skins of CleanYourTV, Aerial, Free My TV and TV Detox repeat the upstream claims. Quiet TV and 简居 TV stay because their READMEs add their own scope.
